stories.summaryEn: The first king lives among the mountains in leopard skins; his son Siamak falls to the demon's son, and Hushang avenges him.
Hushang hurls a stone at a serpent, strikes a spark from the rock and discovers fire; the feast of Sadeh is founded.
Tahmuras rides Ahriman like a horse and binds the demons, who buy their lives by teaching him to write.
Jamshid's golden age of crafts and Nowruz ends in pride; the divine glory leaves him and Zahhak takes his throne.

stories.en: Zahhak the serpent-shouldered and Kaveh the smith
stories.summaryEn: Serpents fed on young men's brains grow from Zahhak's shoulders; Kaveh raises his leather apron as a banner, and Fereydun binds the tyrant on Mount Damavand.
Fereydun divides the world: Rum to Salm, Turan and Chin to Tur, Iran to Iraj. The elder brothers murder Iraj, and the feud of Iran and Turan begins.
Abandoned white-haired child Zal is raised by the Simorgh, loves Rudabeh of Kabul against every objection, and their son Rostam is born.
Afrasiab of Turan invades, captures Nowzar and beheads him; his own brother Aghriras is killed for sparing the Iranian captives.
Young Rostam picks the colt Rakhsh from the herds of Zabol and rides out against Afrasiab.

stories.en: Kay Qobad brought from the Alborz
stories.summaryEn: Rostam fetches Kay Qobad from the Alborz mountains to the empty throne, founding the Kayanian line.
Kay Kavus is blinded and captured in Mazandaran; Rostam rides through seven trials, kills the White Div and heals the king's eyes with its blood.
Kavus marries Sudabeh, daughter of the king of Hamavaran, is imprisoned by her father, freed by Rostam, and later tries to fly to the heavens.
A night in Samangan gives Rostam a son he never meets; years later, neither knowing the other, Rostam kills Sohrab in single combat.
Siavash rides through fire to prove his innocence, crosses into Turan, builds Siavashgerd, and is murdered on Afrasiab's order.
After seven years of searching Turan, Giv finds Siavash's son and brings him and Farangis back across the Jeyhun.
Tus disobeys the king and marches past Kalat, where Kay Khosrow's half-brother Farud is killed and his mother Jarireh dies with him.
The Iranian army is trapped on Mount Hamavan until Rostam arrives and lassos the giant Kamus.
Rostam defeats the allied armies of Turan and the Khaqan of Chin and drags the Khaqan from his white elephant.
A demon in the shape of a wild ass lifts the sleeping Rostam and asks whether to drop him on the mountains or the sea.
Betrayed by Gorgin, Bijan falls in love with Afrasiab's daughter Manijeh and is thrown into a pit under a boulder; Rostam comes disguised as a merchant to free him.
Twelve champions of Iran meet twelve of Turan in single combat at Mount Gonabad; old Goudarz kills Piran.
Kay Khosrow takes Gang Dezh, hunts Afrasiab to a cave and the lake of Chichast, avenges Siavash, then gives up the throne and vanishes into the snow.
Angry with his father Lohrasp, Goshtasp goes to Rum, wins Caesar's daughter Katayun and returns to rule from Balkh.

stories.en: Zoroaster and the war with Arjasp
stories.summaryEn: Goshtasp accepts the faith of Zoroaster; Arjasp of Turan makes war, Zarir falls, and Esfandiyar turns the battle.
To free his sisters, Esfandiyar passes seven trials and takes Arjasp's Brazen Fortress.
Sent to bring Rostam in chains, the invulnerable Esfandiyar is killed by a tamarisk arrow to the eyes, shot on the Simorgh's advice.
His half-brother Shaghad lures Rostam into a pit of spears; dying, Rostam pins him to a tree with one last arrow.
Bahman takes revenge on Rostam's house in Zabol; his daughter Homay sets her infant son Darab adrift in a box on the river.
Darab, raised by a washerman, regains his crown and marries a princess of Rum; their son Dara faces Alexander.
Alexander defeats Dara, then travels the world from India to Mecca, Andalus and the Land of Darkness in search of the water of life, and dies in Babylon.
Ardashir flees Ardavan's court with Golnar, overthrows the last Ashkanian, kills the worm of Haftvad and founds the Sasanian line.
Shapur goes to Rum in disguise, is sewn into an ass's hide by Caesar, escapes with a Roman girl's help and wins back his land.
Raised by the Arabs of Hira, Bahram Gur takes the crown from between two lions, hunts, feasts, and visits Shangul's court in India in disguise.
Mazdak preaches the sharing of wealth and wins King Qobad; the young prince Khosrow destroys him and his followers.
The just king's long reign: wars with Rum, the sage Bozorgmehr, and the games of chess from India and backgammon in reply.
The general Bahram Chubineh crushes Saveh Shah, is insulted by Hormozd, rebels, and drives Khosrow Parviz to seek help from Rum.
Khosrow Parviz brings Shirin to his palace; his son Shiruy kills him, and Shirin takes her life at his tomb.

stories.en: Yazdgerd and the fall of the Sasanians
stories.summaryEn: The Iranian army falls at Qadisiyyah; Yazdgerd flees east and is murdered in a mill near Marv.
